newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Head-on train crash in Luxembourg kills one.
newsitem.headline: Head-on train crash in Luxembourg kills one.

text.p: A passenger and freight train collided head-on in Luxembourg on Sunday, killing one person and injuring nearly 30, seven seriously.
The passenger train, travelling at around 120 km/h (70 mph), hit the freight train about 1.5 km (one mile) south of Luxembourg city station early in the morning.
The driver of the passenger train was killed instantly. The injured were rescued by firemen and taken to hospitals in Luxembourg and Esch-zur-Alzette, a police spokesman said.
Two wagons of the goods train, which was carrying butane gas and bromine among its load, were derailed but no chemicals escaped.
"It's too early to say what the cause of the accident was," Charles-Leon Mayeur, director general of the state railway company SNCFL told RTL-RVI television.
The accident blocked the main line to the south and international trains coming from Italy, Switzerland and France had to be diverted to Arlon in neighbouring Belgium.
The line was expected to remain blocked until Monday morning.
